cohort: 660 women who underwent cesarean delivery at a single center over a two-year period
finding: Use of cyanoacrylate skin glue following subcuticular skin closure at cesarean delivery was associated with a significantly reduced incidence of wound separation and composite wound complications, and a marginal decrease in wound infections.
mod_finding: Cyanoacrylate skin glue may be superior to Steri-strips for wound separation and composite wound complication rates when utilized with subcuticular suture at the time of cesarean delivery and may yield some benefit for prevention of wound infection.
